facts.statement: Bayomesasuchus is an extinct peirosaurid mesoeucrocodylian found in the Cerro Lisandro Formation of Neuquén Province, Argentina.
facts.quote: Bayomesasuchus is an extinct genus of peirosaurid mesoeucrocodylian known from the early Late Cretaceous Cerro Lisandro Formation of Neuquén Province, western central Argentina.

facts.statement: The genus Bayomesasuchus contains only one known species, Bayomesasuchus hernandezi.
facts.quote: It contains a single species, Bayomesasuchus hernandezi.

facts.statement: Despite being known from fragmentary remains, Bayomesasuchus represents one of the most basal peirosaurids.
facts.quote: Even though it is known from relatively fragmentary remains, it represents one of the most basal peirosaurids.

facts.statement: Bayomesasuchus was first described and named by Francisco Barrios, Ariana Paulina-Carabajal, and Paula Bona in 2015.
facts.quote: Bayomesasuchus was first described and named by Francisco Barrios, Ariana Paulina-Carabajal and Paula Bona in 2015

facts.statement: The generic name Bayomesasuchus refers to the Cerro Bayo Mesa mountain in Argentina and 'suchus,' the Greek name for an Egyptian crocodile god.
facts.quote: The generic name refers to the Cero Bayo Mesa mountain, located in southeastern Neuquén Province of Argentina, where the holotype was found, and suchus, Latinized from the Greek souchos, an Egyptian crocodile god.

facts.statement: Bayomesasuchus is known solely from its holotype, which consists of a fragmentary skull and mandible.
facts.quote: Bayomesasuchus is known solely from its holotype, a fragmentary skull and mandible.

facts.statement: Bayomesasuchus lived during the late Cenomanian to early Turonian stages of the early Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: It was collected form the Cerro Lisandro Formation which is the youngest formation within the Río Limay Subgroup, the lowest section of the Neuquén Group, dating to late Cenomanian to early Turonian of the early Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Bayomesasuchus within Peirosauridae in a polytomy with the African species Hamadasuchus rebouli and other South American peirosaurids.
facts.quote: A phylogenetic analysis of Crocodyliformes recovered Bayomesasuchus within Peirosauridae in a polytomy with the African peirosaurid Hamadasuchus rebouli and a clade formed by all other South American peirosaurids.

facts.statement: Bayomesasuchus lived between 93.9 and 89.8 million years ago during the Turonian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Turonian (93.9 to 89.8 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The holotype of Bayomesasuchus is the most complete crocodyliform specimen recorded from the Cerro Lisandro Formation.
rejected.quote: The holotype of Bayomesasuchus is the most complete crocodyliform specimen recorded from the Cerro Lisandro Formation
